hints.title: Maximum Subsequence Sum
hints.text: The largest subsequence sum is the sum of all non-negative numbers. Any other subsequence sum subtracts a subset of absolute values.

hints.title: Sorted Reductions
hints.text: Sort the absolute values of all elements in ascending order. The problem reduces to finding the k-th smallest subsequence sum of these non-negative values.

hints.title: Priority Queue Exploration
hints.text: Use a min-priority queue storing pair (sum, index). Pop the smallest and push transitions to form next candidates without duplicates.

hints.title: Subsequence Reduction Extraction Implementation

complexity.time: O(n log n + k log k)
complexity.notes: Sorting absolute values takes O(n log n), followed by k priority queue extractions.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Enumerating all 2^n subsequences requires exponential time and memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Priority queue bounds candidate storage to at most 2k states.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizes duality between positive sum baseline and k-th smallest absolute reduction.
